note: One row per supported heater model. The single source for every model-dependent number: setpoint range, write-parameter encoding, and identity. gen_profiles.py turns this into src/proto/profiles_gen.h; gen_mqtt.py cross-checks the range against the three places spec/mqtt.json states it before emitting the net-layer constants; python/tests/test_profiles.py pins python/bosch_api.py and spec/api_contract.json to the same numbers. Supporting a new model is a row here plus its A0 golden vectors in spec/protocol_vectors.json - not a firmware edit.

fields.id: stable identifier used in code and generated headers
fields.model: the name Home Assistant shows (home_assistant.device.model in mqtt.json)
fields.a0_frame_type: the A0 payload variant this model broadcasts (0 or 1); selects the parser offsets
fields.setpoint: whole degrees, unit C; the bridge ignores out-of-range commands rather than clamping
fields.write_param: the D3 write-frame body prefix: parameter type, parameter id, index - then the value in whole degrees
fields.status: verified = driven on real hardware; expected = protocol believed identical, awaiting a contributor

names: Therm 4800i (EU import of the same unit, unverified)
profiles.setpoint_note: The A0 state frame itself reports max_setpoint (payload[33] & 0x7F); the captured value is 60 and the profile agrees, so firmware that ever disagrees with the heater is a build failure here, not a runtime surprise.
profiles.write_param_note: Byte-identical to python/bosch_api.set_temperature and to the d3_set_temperature_42 golden vector in spec/protocol_vectors.json; the C++ self test rebuilds that vector from this row.
